content:
mira: Heads up — we've been getting a bunch of dcgm_xid and ECC spikes in us-west-2 tonight, ~70 alerts in the past 2 hours. SRE queue is noisy. Can we tune Prom rules to reduce noise but still catch real flakey cards?

kai: Yeah saw that. Most are 1-off spikes that self-clear. Current rule fires on `increase(dcgm_xid_error_count[5m]) > 0`. Too sensitive.

sanjay: Agree. We should switch to a streak-based rule (e.g., 3 windows out of 5 > threshold) and also group by `node`+`gpu_index` so we don't aggregate across cards.

lara: Also worth suppressing alerts for nodes with recent driver updates — post-driver-rollout noise was high last week. Add `unless on(node) node_last_driver_update_timestamp > time() - 86400` or label-based suppression.

mira: Good point. We also saw most noisy cards are older A100s with specific firmware. Can we add metadata tags (driver, firmware, instance_type) to the recording rules so paging is actionable?

kai: Yes — having `gpu_driver_version` and `pci_id` labels in the recording rule helps routing.

ops-bot: alert: DCGM_XID_HIGH node=ip-10-2-45-12 gpu=1 count=3 window=15m

lara: Proposed rule (recording + alerting) — this would suppress single blips and prefer a consecutive-window pattern:

```yaml
# recording: per-card xid rate per 5m window
- record: infra:gpu:dcgm_xid_increase:5m
  expr: increase(dcgm_xid_error_count[5m])
  labels:
    job: "dcgm-exporter"
    severity: "info"

# alert: fire if 3 out of 5 windows in last 25m exceed 0
- alert: GPU_XID_Streak
  expr: (
    sum_over_time((infra:gpu:dcgm_xid_increase:5m > 0)[25m:5m]) >= 3
  )
  for: 0m
  labels:
    severity: "warning"
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU {{ $labels.node }}:{{ $labels.gpu_index }} XID streaks"
    runbook: "https://redwood-internal/ops/playbooks/gpu-triage"
```

kai: I like that. `sum_over_time(...[25m:5m]) >= 3` basically counts how many windows had >0 and alerts if 3+. Cleaner than `increase` single-window checks.

sanjay: We should also make a separate alert for ECC counts where any single window > 5 should fire (ECC is more severe). For ECC:

```promql
infra:gpu:dcgm_ecc_increase:5m = increase(dcgm_ecc_corrected_error_count[5m])
```

and alert: `infra:gpu:dcgm_ecc_increase:5m > 5` with `for: 10m` so transient spikes don't page immediately.

mira: Runbook additions: when the streak alert fires -> 1) check `dmesg` for GPU Xid lines, 2) `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets` suggested only after 2 consecutive alerts, 3) if driver/firmware mismatch, schedule rolling reboot. Add a quick repro: run a small stress job to see if XIDs reproduce.

lara: Also propose labeling MIG presence: if `gpu_mig_enabled == 1` then escalate differently (MIG containers may surface errors without full card fail).

kai: Another practical noise filter: ignore alerts from nodes that were cordoned/drained in the last hour (we reimage and cause metric churn). Use `node_maintenance_state` label from inventory.

sanjay: Ops suggestion: Add a short-term debounce in Alertmanager — group by `node,gpu_index` and add a `repeat_interval` of 30m for same firing alert to cut down duplicates. But keep critical ECC alerts with no debounce.

mira: Can we also emit a `gpu_error_streak_count` recording rule so the console dashboards can show trending? Ops wants a 7d rolling count per gpu.

lara: Yep — simple `sum_over_time((infra:gpu:dcgm_xid_increase:5m > 0)[7d:5m])` -> record.

ops-bot: suggestion: auto-tag nodes in alert body with `driver`, `firmware`, `instance_type`, `mig` to help triage.

kai: One more thing — for very noisy cards we should auto-suppress alerts into a special queue and create a ticket to replace/label them (avoid pager fatigue). Criteria: >10 streak alerts in 7d -> escalate to `hardware-replacement` queue.

mira: Sounds good. Action items:
- lara: PR with recording+alerting rules (streak + ECC exceptions) — include labels: node,gpu_index,gpu_driver_version,pci_id (due EOD).
- kai: Update Alertmanager grouping/repeat_interval and route for ECC (tomorrow morning).
- sanjay: Add inventory label exports (driver+firmware+mig) from the node exporter / inventory exporter (this week).
- mira: Draft runbook updates and replacement criteria, then sync with oncall to test (this afternoon).

oncall-rotation: acked — I'll monitor the queue and silence noisy alerts during the rollout. :thumbsup:

mira: Thanks everyone — let's keep the initial pr lightweight and iterate. If anyone wants to pair on the PromQL I can be free in 15.
